title.narrative: Employment for young men and women through entrepreneurship, Value Chain Development, green enterprises, social enterprises and cooperatives and business development programmes promoted

description.narrative: In response to challenges arising from the growing refugee population in Egypt—and their vulnerabilities and the pressures placed on host communities—the Netherlands launched the PROSPECTS initiative, in partnership with the IFC, ILO, UNHCR, UNICEF, and the World Bank. Building on a first phase concluding in December 2024, PROSPECTS Egypt will continue through 2027 to enhance living standards and inclusivity for refugees, asylum-seekers, and vulnerable host populations across Greater Cairo, Alexandria, and Damietta. The initiative centers on four key pillars: - Expanding access to quality education, skills training, and learning opportunities for forcibly displaced persons (FDPs) and host communities (HCs). - Strengthening livelihoods and economic prospects through entrepreneurship and dignified employment. - Increasing government protection and fostering greater inclusion in local, community-based, and national social protection systems. - Improving services, infrastructure, and information systems essential to FDPs and HCs. The DECENT WORK FOR WOMEN project—supported by EBRD—enables employer organizations in Egypt, Tunisia, and Morocco to train their members, particularly women, for the green transition. Its curriculum spans green business innovation, certification, finance, and sector-specific guidance for women-led enterprises. The PE4DW Egypt project, funded by the Italian Agency and implemented with Egypt’s Ministry of Trade and Industry, supports productivity and decent work in the leather and marble sectors. It assists 200 SMEs in overcoming productivity barriers and improving working conditions.
